answer: Each agent must earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomized, independently checked tasks before it can influence high-value decisions. The checks draw on a shared inlet of fresh tasks, while a walnut-sized bond is forfeited when a result fails verification; repeated success gradually raises the agent’s voting weight. A Sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each must spend time and capital building its own reputation, and one failed batch can burn the bond without letting the attacker transfer credibility along a thread of disposable accounts.
